Glossary — what everything means

Out of stock / Low stock / Adequate
Stock status based on how many days your current stock will last at current sales speed. Out of stock = 0 units. Low stock = less than 30 days of cover. Adequate = 30+ days.
Days cover
How many days your current stock will last based on average daily sales. "46d" means at current demand, you'll run out in about 46 days.
Velocity
How fast a medicine sells. Measured in units per month. A "FAST" medicine sells many units; a "SLOW" one sells very few.
Trend ▲ / ▼
Whether sales are going up or down compared to the same month last year. "▲ 86%" means sales are 86% higher than the same month last year.
Suggested reorder
The recommended quantity to order. Calculated from sales speed × (delivery time + target coverage days) + safety buffer − current stock.
ABC Classification (Priority / Standard / Low)
Priority (A) = Top medicines generating 80% of your revenue. Never let these run out. Standard (B) = Mid-range, 15% of revenue. Low (C) = Bottom 5% of revenue — consider if you need to keep stocking them.
XYZ Classification (Stable / Variable / Erratic)
Stable (X) = Demand is predictable month to month. Easy to order. Variable (Y) = Demand changes but has some pattern. Keep extra stock. Erratic (Z) = Demand is unpredictable. Hardest to manage.
Margin %
Your profit percentage. "8.7%" means for every AED 100 of sales, you keep AED 8.70 as profit.
Effective cost
The real price you pay after accounting for bonuses. If you buy 10 and get 1 free, the effective cost per unit is lower than the invoice price.
Bonus margin
Your profit margin when calculated using the effective cost (after bonus), which is more accurate than using the invoice price.
Fill rate
The percentage of your medicines that are in stock. 75% fill rate means 75% of items are available for customers.
EBP (Essential Benefits Package)
Medicines covered by UAE health insurance. These typically have higher demand because patients get them covered by their insurance plan.
DDC (Dubai Drug Code)
A unique registration code assigned to every medicine approved for sale in Dubai. Used for regulatory tracking.
Regulated price / MRP
The maximum price set by the UAE government. Selling above this price is a compliance violation.
Salt / Generic name
The active ingredient in the medicine. Multiple brands can contain the same salt — these are alternatives patients can switch between.
Same salt alternatives
Other medicines in your stock with the same active ingredient. Useful when one brand is out of stock — you can suggest an alternative to the customer.
Dead stock
Medicines sitting in your warehouse with no sales for 3+ months. This is money tied up that could be used elsewhere.
Stockout cost
Estimated revenue lost because a medicine is out of stock. Calculated from daily demand × selling price × days out of stock.
MRN (Material Receipt Note)
A record of goods received from a supplier. Used to track purchase history and reconcile orders.
PO (Purchase Order)
A document sent to a supplier to order medicines. The dashboard tracks POs to know what's been ordered and what's been received.
Notes vs Action taken
Action taken is a structured status (Ordered, Pending, etc.) that drives reports and order tracking. Notes is free-text just for your own reference — like "Called supplier Monday" — and never affects any calculation, filter, or report. Keep day-to-day context in Notes, keep official workflow status in Action taken.
Min/Max par levels
Manually set minimum and maximum stock levels for a medicine. When stock drops below the minimum, you get an alert to reorder. When stock is above the maximum, it suggests reducing stock. Set these in the medicine detail panel.
Near-expiry return
Medicines approaching their expiry date that can potentially be returned to the supplier for credit or replacement. Items with 90+ days to expiry are usually eligible for return. Use the action "Writing for Expiry Replacement" to flag items for return.
Seasonal demand
Medicines that sell significantly more in one half of the year (winter vs summer). The "Winter peak" or "Summer peak" badge tells you to stock up before that season. When a peak season is 1-2 months away or currently active, the suggested reorder quantity automatically increases (+30% in the run-up to the season, +15% during the season itself) to help you avoid running out during high demand.
